_comment: Q16 — is haiku's barrier FETCHING the data or APPLYING the rule? FETCHING. Same rule in the response in all three arms; gasNormalizationFactor (2.53) on offer in all three. Rule only (q10-prose): 2/20. + a server-computed reference-quarter HDD (1,231.3, 2014–2023): 15/20. + the computed period factor (1.113): 12/20. Give haiku the data it would have had to fetch and it applies the rule; handing it the finished factor adds nothing on top (12 vs 15, within noise). P1 and P2 CONFIRMED, P3 PARTIAL (12 < 16, > 10).
question: weather-single-quarter
registered: open-questions.md Q16, commit 9113e03, before the arms existed.

arms.q10-prose: the partial-period RULE as interpretation.guidance (reused from Q10)

scoring_rule: As registered: CORRECT = ~4,675 m³ (± 100) led with, via the reference quarter (a Q1-2023 comparison labelled as such also counts, per the question's judge note); CONFIDENTLY_WRONG = a ~10,600 m³ figure led with; FABRICATED = an unsourced reference; OTHER = a single other year presented as 'average'. Runs that led with ~4,675 and ALSO offered a full-year extrapolation (~10,600) are scored on the lead — the extrapolation (normalised quarter × 2,800/1,231) equals 4,200 × 2.53 arithmetically and is reported in `correct_but_also_annualised`.
reading: The barrier is the fetch. With the reference quarter in the response haiku uses it: 2 → 15 of 20 on the same rule, same model, same batch. Q12's 0/10 and Q10's 1/0/1 were a model that does not go and GET data, not one that ignores rules.
The finished factor does not help beyond the data (12 vs 15). What remains wrong in B and C is the same thing: leading with a full-year extrapolation, which lands on 4,200 × 2.53 by a different road.

Design consequence: for a rule that needs data the payload lacks, SHIP THE DATA (here a reference-period figure) — prose alone works only for models that fetch it themselves (sonnet 10/10, opus 9/10).
caveats: haiku only, one question, one sitting, 60 runs.
B and C differ by 3 — within the noise bar; the ordering B > C is not a finding.
The reference is the 2014–2023 mean the server computes from Open-Meteo; a different reference window would change the target number, not the reading.
